I come there a few times to make test results, but for some reason, they are lazy print these results, even when you pay for it! They charge 1900 baht and accept Japanese negative test certificates.

This is the cheapest place in Pattaya (900B) to take a PCR test for returning to Japan. The hospital seems to be used to dealing with Japanese people, so they are quick to respond. You have to go twice because you have to pick up the results the next day, but it's not a problem because you can easily get there by songthaew (the last stop) from Pattaya city. It takes about 15 minutes in total from filling out the paperwork and paying to finishing the test. It's cheap and fast, so there's nothing to complain about. (However, this is only if the result is negative.)

If you do a PCR test on Friday, you will receive it on Saturday. However, it is closed on Sundays and public holidays.

You can get a PCR test for 900B. It's very convenient as it's near the market!
The test itself only takes 5 minutes.
The next day, when I went to the counter at the front entrance, there was an envelope containing the test results.
I highly recommend this place if you're leaving Thailand!

text: You can get a PCR test certificate for returning home for 900 baht. It takes two days for the test and collection (the next day). There is no collection time, so just enter the time on My SOS as 0:01.

PCR test done
Vaccine passport done
Very impressed with the service. Staff are polite and able to speak english.

This was my first time using their service. It's located next to Naklua Market. They were very helpful and gave me clear directions. If you're worried, I recommend going in advance and getting an application form. It's cheap, reliable, and fast.

Visited on May 24, 2022.

I arrived at 8:30 AM, the opening time, but there were only four people there.
Even by 9 AM, when the PCR test was over, there were only about 10 people there.
However, there's no guarantee that it will remain this crowded.

All you need to bring is your passport. They'll make a copy of your passport there anyway. Of course, bringing a copy will speed up the process.

They also give you a questionnaire, so just fill out the circled sections. It takes about 10 minutes.

And even if you fill out the questionnaire quickly, you still have to wait for your turn. They always do the PCR test in order.

The PCR test is very quick. They tell you to come pick up your results at 10:30 AM the next day. You'll be given your passport and receipt, which you should also bring.

The price is 900 baht. Cash only.

If you have time afterward, it would be nice to buy shrimp at the seafood market right next door and eat them on a mat. If you pay on the side, they'll cook it for you. Personally, I recommend the 300-400 baht per kilo.
Went on Saturday morning to get my vaccination passport. There were hardly any people. You can walk in. Good service but a bit slow because there was only one queue.

If you have a flight the next day, don't go in the morning. Go at 12:30 PM. You'll be the first one to get tested at 1:00 PM. Fill out the questionnaire upon arrival. You'll receive your test papers at 2:30 PM the next day.
I took a songthaew from in front of Walking Street, and since I was the only one on board, they let me choose my route at Terminal 21. So I went to the fish market for 10 baht.

Didn't take so long.
It took less than 30minutes to get PCR test.
It didn't hurt that much :)

Anyone needs their RT-PCR Test done, this is the cheapest place to be! 900 Baht for RT PCR.

However, they’re always closed on Sundays and Public Holidays. Always check Thai Calendar. 🙏🏼

Since I heard it starts at 8:30 AM, I decided to go a bit early and wait. I arrived around 8:05 AM, but the doors were already open and the PCR testing area was accepting people. I received number 4.

However, a woman came running almost as if she were trying to overtake me with only a 2-3 second gap. I was about to yield but decided against it. So, she couldn't overtake me.

(This is where the twist begins.)

But it turned out she was a travel agency employee who had brought Korean tourists. While I was getting my number, about 40 Koreans who had been on two minibuses rushed in. It turned out she was a local travel agency employee trying to get ahead of everyone else and register as a group first.

Because of that 2-3 second difference, I almost ended up with number 44 instead of 4.

It is really wise to go early and wait.

If you are unlucky enough to be later than the travel agency shuttle, there is no hope. After that, several foreigners kept coming in as well.

I recommend going as early as possible.

They ask for a copy of your passport when you get your number; bringing it speeds things up a bit, but if you don't... they just make a copy for you there.

I also heard that a plane ticket is required, so I printed out my airline e-ticket and brought it, but they weren't interested in it at all and it wasn't needed.

They give you a paperwork form clipped to fill out. It's a questionnaire asking for your English name, nationality, occupation, address, whether you have COVID symptoms, whether you work in the medical field related to COVID-19, whether you came from a high-risk area for confirmed cases, etc., so most people end up checking "no."

You just need to fill out your vaccination history, the name of the shot, and where you received it. I wrote it incorrectly and crossed it out with lines, but they said it didn't matter.

I was too lazy to write the name of the hospital where I got vaccinated in English on the site, so I just wrote "hospital," but they later corrected it to "Korea Hospital."

They overlook pretty much everything. ^^;

I thought I would just clip my number, passport copy, and completed documents together and start right away, but I had to wait again.

I sat in a chair like that until it started at 8:30.

When it was my turn, they called out the number.

After confirming my number at the table next to where I initially received it, they reviewed my completed documents and passport copy, made necessary corrections, and asked for 900 baht. After paying in cash, they gave me a stamped receipt.

(You can pick up your results the next day using that receipt, so please keep it safe.)

Then, I moved to a chair at the table right next to it. There, they re-checked my documents, stamped them, and said everything was done.

I took that to the staff table near the waiting area. After reviewing my documents, they wrote my name on the test reagents and cotton swabs, and told me to take them and sit in the very front chair in that waiting area.

Once there, I went to the testing chair in order to receive the test. One oral test, one nasal test.

And that was it. It was around 8:50 when I finished everything.

The process was on the slow side.

When I asked on my way out, they told me to come back the next day at 10:30 to pick up the results. The email service was discontinued after the price changed to 900 baht.

It costs 3,500 baht at the International Hospital in downtown Pattaya.

A certain YouTube video claimed that if you book through a travel agency at a certain hotel, it costs 1,900 baht, so I asked that agency directly, and they said it was 2,400 baht. The price has gone up.

And here, it's 900 baht.

It's a profit even if you take a Bolt Taxi for a round trip for two days.

When I received the results the next day, it showed that I was tested at 11:00 the previous day, and the printout indicated the results came out at 5:00 PM the previous day.

Therefore, since the time starts counting from the day before the test, make sure to time your return within 48 hours. I hope you get tested cheaply and use the remaining money to treat yourself to something delicious one more time. I wish you a great trip! ^^

PCR test 900 baht.
I went as soon as the doors opened, and there were about 20 people waiting. It's best to take a number, fill out the form, and then wait.
The test took about an hour.
Results will be available in person the next day.

This is the most affordable PCR testing center in Pattaya.

The service costs 1,500 baht, and you will receive an email around 10 AM tomorrow after the test is completed on the same day.

Friendly staffs especially the senior lady  in reception

You can ask the nearby restaurants to cook your seafood, but the cooking methods are a bit strange and might not suit Chinese tastes. However, it's a great tourist attraction, and if you don't mind the mess, you can give it a visit!
